title: crosslang: add retry-orchestration + auth-plugin + stream ergonomic helpers; bump sdks
author: Samir Patel
description:
Motivation: multiple downstream teams reported mismatches between SDK retry behavior and server-side backoff hints during stream reconnects, and a recurring flake in token refresh ordering. This PR introduces a cross-language "retry orchestration" surface plus a small auth-plugin interface that lets SDKs opt into server-driven backoff windows and coordinate token refresh during streaming handoffs. The goal is to provide a single, testable behavior across Python/TypeScript/Go without forcing a large rewrite of existing public APIs.

What this PR does (high level):
- Introduces an AuthPlugin interface and lightweight adapter in each SDK that centralizes refresh semantics and exposes a jittered backoff window derived from server hints.
- Adds a RetryOrchestrator helper that consumes backoff hints + client-side policy (max attempts, total timeout) and emits a compact retry plan used by streaming helpers.
- Adds ergonomics helpers for streaming consumers: Python context-manager for resumable streams, TypeScript async-generator wrapper with backpressure hints, and Go PullStream convenience helpers.
- Implements a small compatibility shim so older SDK users keep their current semantics unless they opt into the new orchestrator via a single config flag.
- Bumps SDK versions: python -> 1.12.0, typescript -> 1.27.4, go -> 1.8.2 and updates CHANGELOGs.

Migration notes: opt-in via client config (e.g., client = Client(auth_plugin=..., retry_orchestrator_enabled=True)). Applications that rely on legacy immediate-refresh-on-401 behavior should test with the opt-in flag before switching globally.

Testing and validation: unit tests added for the orchestrator logic in each SDK, cross-SDK integration test that simulates interleaved token refreshes + reconnects, and a new flaky-stream CI job to hold regressions. Performance impact: negligible on hot paths; orchestrator decisions happen on reconnect paths only.

Rollout plan: feature gated by default off; ops will enable for selected tenants in staged rollout after a week of canary monitoring.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc linked in Linear (ENG-2127)
- [x] Unit tests for orchestrator and auth plugin (py/ts/go)
- [x] Integration test that reproduces previous race and shows fix
- [x] Docs + CHANGELOG entries
- [x] Version bumps and publish scripts updated

review_thread:
Lena Ortiz: REQUEST CHANGES – observed a potential race where python's refresh coroutine could interleave with the reconnect handler and cause duplicate refreshes; please add a deterministic unit test and consider a lightweight mutex.

Samir Patel (author): Thanks – added a deterministic reproducer and a small sequentialization step in the python adapter (commit f7a8e22). The change keeps the public API the same and is guarded behind the opt-in flag.

Maya Chen: Suggested tightening TS types for the backoff window (min/max) and adding a short example in the TS examples folder. Also asked for a small note in the Python docs highlighting the context-manager semantics.

Samir: Addressed both; added types and an example (c8d9a33) and expanded docs.

Thomas Fischer: Approves after verifying go adapter respects existing credential interfaces and does not change semantics when the orchestrator is disabled.

CI: initial run failed in flaky-stream-integration (timeout in test harness) — root cause was the test harness awaiting a reconnect that wasn't triggered; adjusted the harness timing and reran. Final run green.
merge_outcome: merged via squash commit; release preparations for SDK publish started (abridged commit message created during squash).
release_notes: Added a new opt-in Retry Orchestrator and Auth Plugin across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs. This enables server-driven backoff windows for more consistent stream reconnect behavior and reduces token refresh races during streaming. Opt-in by default; see docs/sdk/migration_guide_retry_orchestrator.md for migration steps. SDK versions bumped: python 1.12.0, typescript 1.27.4, go 1.8.2.
